title: Syrians grow frustrated as soaring living costs threaten recovery
summary:
People burned tyres, blocked roads and chanted slogans, angry at the government's decision to raise fuel prices again.
It was the largest show of discontent yet since President Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power two years ago.
But as they celebrated Assad's overthrow and their new freedoms, Syrians, perhaps unrealistically, hoped things would quickly improve.
And many saw a further and unexpected rise in fuel prices as a sign of a government out of touch with its country.

title: Europe's youth are protesting - and feeling locked out of a future
summary:
From Milan, to Marseille, to Madrid and in so many other cities across Europe, streets have erupted in colourful, passionate protests in recent weeks.
While most started peacefully, a large number ended in shocking scenes of violence and looting.
In Lisbon, tens of thousands of mostly young people marched earlier this month.
In Albania, demonstrators alleging government corruption are demanding that their Prime Minister Edi Rama - already 13 years in power - stand down.
I've spent years in Europe reporting from a multitude of demonstrations, both peaceful and violent.

title: King Charles in Guyana as Bahamas visit declared 'diplomatic success'
summary:

The main themes of the two-day state visit to Guyana will be the environment and sustainability - alongside the growing commercial ties between the UK and Guyana.
Guyana - formerly British Guiana - is the world's fastest growing economy due to the discovery of oil reserves there in 2015.

The two-day trip to the Bahamas saw the King meet young boxers, environmentalists and politicians.

title: Syria-Jordan border reopens amid probe into deadly air strikes
summary:
Foreign ministers form security committee to share intelligence and follow up on impact of Jordan’s strikes on Syria.
Syria is reopening its border crossing with Jordan, and the two countries will investigate Jordanian strikes on suspected ISIL (ISIS) sites that killed seven in southern Syria.
Jordan’s strikes on Syria killed at least seven people in Deraa and Suwayda, including five members of the same family, three of whom were children.
Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi said Monday’s air attacks were based on field intelligence and aimed at “neutralising confirmed threats and imminent terrorist operations targeting Jordan’s security”.
Jordanian security forces arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law on suspicion of carrying out the attack.

title: Serbia: Student-backed election winners demand sweeping resignations
summary:
Serbia's victorious student-led movement has called for top figures in the police, intelligence and judiciary to stand down, days after ousting ex-president Aleksandar Vučić's party from power.
Standing in Pioneers' Park opposite parliament, newly elected MPs on the Student List demanded the immediate dismissal of all police officers who had broken the law, singling out the heads of the police, the BIA security agency and anti-terror unit.
But the handover of power will take weeks, and the students' movement is concerned that evidence of possible wrongdoing could be destroyed in that time.
Just a few days ago, the park they were standing in on Thursday was a tent camp, filled with Vučić loyalists outside his office.
Within hours of him admitting defeat on Sunday night, the camp was dismantled, and a team of volunteers moved in on Monday morning to clean up the mess.
